explanations.text:
import json, the system, the pattern matcher, the shell, a lock, the clock, and two neighbours:
[the tool](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py) — the project folder, the map of a file —
and [the project hand](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py), which knows the word project and its map

FOLDER = server — the folder under human/ where a writing from the reader waits
KINDS  = the six kinds of writing: retext, map, code, expand, create, delete
WRITTEN = the five kinds that carry words of your own: retext, map, code, expand, create
ENTRY_RE = the look of the line "entry 3: …" the map command prints, so the new number can be read back


[save_writing](save_writing)(root, name, kind, eid, text, words)
    root is the project folder; 
    name of the abstraction. which goes as input to [name_to_map()](compiler/cli/human/helpers.py:name_to_map); 
    kind is one of the six the
    reader may send; eid is
    the entry the words replace, or the entry an ask stands on, or
    nothing; text is what you typed in the reader and sent with the
    save button, and it may be empty on a delete; words are the words
    you highlighted in an entry for an expand.

    ●  the tool checks the ask
    │     An unknown kind stops here. An empty text stops the five kinds
    │     that carry your words; only a delete may come with no text
    │     at all. 
    |     A name of the sort type file must be a real file under the project root, and not under human/
    │     A name of the sort type project or human file has no file, so those two checks do not run.
    │     The map .json of the name is read; it may not exist yet. A map
    │     that holds no entries counts as no map in the checks below.
    │
    ●  the tool runs the same command you would have typed          ([the command run](run_cli))
    │     A rewrite of an entry runs human retext <name> <id> --verbatim:
    │     your words go in as your own, the origin is reset, and the
    │     entries that stood on the old words are marked stale. A first
    │     telling runs human map <name> --verbatim: plain words, a pin in
    │     them refused; on a file that has a map already the run stops —
    │     write on its entries instead. Code on a file with no map is
    │     written to the file as it is; on a file with a map the run stops,
    │     because the words come first there.
    │
    ●  an expand or a create writes your words as a new entry
    │     A create writes a top abstraction over an entry. An expand
    │     writes more words under the words you highlighted, and stops
    │     when no words came with it. A create and an expand stop when
    │     the map holds no such entry. Both run human map <name>
    │     --verbatim, so your words go in at once and the mark
    │     carries the new entry with it.
    │
    ●  a delete takes the entry out at once and queues nothing
    │     It stops when the map holds no such entry. Otherwise it runs
    │     human undo <name> --entry <id>: the entry leaves the map, and the
    │     run stops when another entry, or the project map, points at it
    │     through an anchor. A not-compiled mark that waits on the entry is
    │     dropped too. The reader gets what the command said, joined
    │     in one line, without the line that names the written map.
    │
    ●  a refusal goes back to the reader in the command's own words
    │     The gates are the same as on the command line. Nothing is marked
    │     when a gate speaks.
    │
    
  the tool looks for the abstractions that stand on a code write        ([the pins that reach a file](pins_reaching))
  every map is read for a pin that names the file: the map of each file, the project map and every human file.
  if no pin the file is just saved and gets no mark because no abstraction depends on it. 
  if pins, the write is marked; at compile the pins go into the event, so the ai harness knows which abstractions the change may have made wrong.
    
    │
    ●  the writing is marked as not compiled                          ([the mark](mark))
          The kind, the name, the entry number — read from the output for a first telling, an expand or a create —,
          and the old text go into human/server/not_compiled.json.
          An expand or a create adds the entry it stands on as its target, an expand adds
          the highlighted words, and the output says which entry it
          expands or stands over.
          A second save on the same entry, or on the same code, while the first mark
          still waits adds no new mark, so the first old text holds.
          The reader gets the entry number and the printed lines. Nothing joins the
          queue until you push the compile button.

[compile_saved](compile_saved)(root, name)
    name is the abstraction whose compile button you pushed.

    ●  the tool makes one event from each waiting mark of the name    ([the event of a mark](event_of))
    │     The kind, the name, the absolute paths of the map and the file,
    │     the entry number, the old text, and the new text as it is now in the map or the file.
    │     A code write carries the pins that reach the file; an expand or a create carries its
    │     target, and an expand its highlighted words.
    │     A mark gives no event and is dropped when its entry is gone or its text is the old text
    │     again, or when no pin reaches the code now or the file is gone.
    │
    ●  each event joins the queue                                     ([the queue](append_event))
          The mark keeps the number of its event, so the reader knows it is compiling.
          The reader gets the event numbers and how many went to the ai harness,
          or that nothing saved waits for a compile.

[cmd_watch](cmd_watch)(a)
    a is what you typed: human watch, or human watch --once.

    ●  claude arms it once per session, from the project root
    │     Every event not yet done is printed, one JSON line each, in the
    │     order it came. An event printed in an earlier session comes with
    │     maybe_started true, so claude checks the maps before it syncs anything.
    │
    ●  the tool follows
          Every second it reads the queue again ([the events](read_events)) and prints
          what is new. The cursor's seen mark moves to the last printed
          event ([the cursor](read_cursor)). With --once it prints and stops.

[cmd_ack](cmd_ack)(a)
    a holds the number of the event claude finished: human ack 3.

    ●  the tool moves the done mark
          The number must be above the last done and not beyond the last
          event; otherwise the tool says what is done and what is last.
          The not-compiled marks whose events are now done are dropped.
          Then it says how many events still wait. The reader drops the
          compiling mark of the entry when the queue tells it the event is done.

[pending](pending)(root)
    ●  the reader asks what still waits
          The done and seen marks, and one line per event above done: its
          number, kind, name, and entry; and every not-compiled mark: its name,
          kind, entry, and the number of its event once it is sent. The reader
          polls this to mark an entry as not compiled or compiling.



# HELPER FUNCTIONS

[folder](folder)(root)                        
 human/server/ under the root, made on first use

[events_path](events_path)(root)              
 the queue file, events.jsonl

[cursor_path](cursor_path)(root)              
 the cursor file, cursor.json

[read_events](read_events)(root)              
 every event of the queue, oldest first

[read_cursor](read_cursor)(root)              
 the done and seen marks; zero and zero when none

[write_cursor](write_cursor)(root, c)         
 writes the marks back

[append_event](append_event)(root, event)     
 numbers the event one above the last, stamps the moment, adds it

[run_cli](run_cli)(root, args, text)          
 runs the human command in the project folder with the text on its stdin; gives back whether it passed and what it printed. When human is one built program, it runs that program itself; otherwise it runs human through python. On windows the command runs with no console window, so no black window opens on each compile

[pins_reaching](pins_reaching)(root, name)
 every pin of every map that names the file: the map, the entry, the words, and the block or anchor it points at

[marks_path](marks_path)(root)
 the not-compiled file, not_compiled.json

[read_marks](read_marks)(root)
 every not-compiled mark; none when the file is missing or broken

[write_marks](write_marks)(root, marks)
 writes the marks back through a temporary file with the process id in its name

[slot](slot)(m)
 what makes two marks the same: the name, code or not, and the entry

[mark](mark)(root, m)
 adds a not-compiled mark, unless a mark in the same slot still waits

[unmark](unmark)(root, name, eid)
 drops the waiting marks of one entry
